title: Adaptive Fidelity Client Negotiation API - Design Spec
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

Purpose: Define a stable, forward-compatible API that enables client applications to declare cost- and latency-sensitivity at request time and participate in a runtime negotiation with Redwood Inference to select an execution fidelity profile. This specification covers the API surface, negotiation semantics, default policies, observability hooks, and a rollout plan.

Context: Redwood supports multiple fidelity trade-offs (model variant, quantization, batching behavior, KV cache usage, streaming vs. non-streaming). Today fidelity is determined server-side via routing policies and per-tenant configuration. For certain latency-sensitive or cost-sensitive integrations it is beneficial for clients to express their tolerance and preferred trade-offs per-request. The Adaptive Fidelity Client Negotiation API formalizes that contract while preserving server-side safety and economic controls.

Goals
- Provide a compact request-level contract for expressing cost/latency/quality sensitivity.
- Allow runtime negotiation responses that are deterministic and auditable.
- Enable economical defaults for unauthenticated or legacy clients.
- Integrate cleanly with billing and SLO bookkeeping.

Non-goals
- This spec does not define every fidelity knob (internal kernel selection or micro-quantization configs remain server-only).
- Not intended to replace tenant-level SLA/contract negotiation for Dedicated/Private installs.

Terminology
- Fidelity Profile: a named set of runtime choices (model variant, quantization level, batching class, streaming mode, KV cache policy).
- Cost Sensitivity: client-declared preference on price vs. quality/latency (enum: low|medium|high).
- Latency Constraint: explicit per-request max latency SLO (ms) or a tier (realtime|interactive|background).
- Negotiation Response: server's chosen fidelity profile + metadata & pricing delta.

High-level design
1) Clients supply an optional fidelityHint object on generation/embedding/chat requests. If omitted, server applies tenant defaults.
2) Server evaluates requested constraints against platform policies, capacity, and customer contract.
3) Server returns a negotiation result immediately (synchronous) or a provisional result (when long-running prefetch/compile is needed) and encodes the chosen fidelity in the response header/body.
4) Execution proceeds under the chosen fidelity profile; cost and telemetry attribute to the selected profile.

API contract
- Endpoint: POST /v1/infer (existing) — expanded contract; alternate dedicated endpoint: POST /v1/fidelity-negotiate for preflight checks.
- New request field (optional): fidelityHint (object)

Example JSON (embedded in request body):

```
{
  "input": "Summarize the quarterly results",
  "model": "redwood-rlhf-13b",
  "fidelityHint": {
    "costSensitivity": "medium",
    "latencyTier": "interactive",
    "minQualityScore": 0.82,
    "preferStreaming": true,
    "acceptableVariants": ["redwood-13b-q8_0", "redwood-13b-q4_0"],
    "fallbackPolicy": "best-effort"  
  }
}
```

Field reference (table):

Name | Type | Description | Default
-----|------|-------------|--------
costSensitivity | string | low|medium|high. Controls willingness to accept cheaper variants. | medium
latencyTier | string | realtime|interactive|background. Maps to target p95 latency. | interactive
minQualityScore | number | 0.0-1.0. Client-specified lower bound on model quality (normalized eval metric). | 0.7
preferStreaming | boolean | Prefers streaming tokens as they are produced. May increase cost. | false
acceptableVariants | list[string] | Ordered preference list of model variant ids acceptable to client. | []
fallbackPolicy | string | best-effort|guarantee-min-quality|cost-first. Controls server fallback behavior. | best-effort

Negotiation response (returned in body and headers):
- fidelityProfile (string): canonical profile id used for execution (e.g., r-13b-q8-batched-realtime).
- effectivePriceMultiplier (number): multiplicative factor applied to base unit price for telemetry/billing.
- expectedP95 (ms): expected p95 latency under selected profile.
- qualityEstimate (0-1): server-side estimate of quality normalized to the requested metric.
- negotiatedFlags: list of server-side applied flags (e.g., kv_cache_disabled, small_batch_mode).
- negotiationTraceId: opaque id used for audit and debugging.

Example response snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Fidelity-Profile: r-13b-q4-smallbatch
X-RW-Negotiation-Trace: trace_20260621_45ab
{
  "fidelityProfile": "r-13b-q4-smallbatch",
  "effectivePriceMultiplier": 0.75,
  "expectedP95": 220,
  "qualityEstimate": 0.78,
  "negotiatedFlags": ["kv_cache_reduced"],
  "negotiationTraceId": "trace_20260621_45ab"
}
```

Authorization and policy enforcement
- Request-level negotiation is allowed only if tenant contract permits per-request modifiers. For Hosted free-tier tenants, negotiation is read-only and returns conservative profiles.
- The platform evaluates requests against: per-tenant quotas, region capacity, active incidents, and model marketplace licensing.
- Admin override: operators can set a global enforcement policy that disables client-specified fallbacks during emergency states.

Negotiation semantics and deterministic behavior
- Determinism: the server must compute the negotiation outcome using deterministic inputs (tenant id, fidelityHint, time-bucket, current capacity watermark). Document deterministic tie-breaking order: 1) explicit acceptableVariants list, 2) costSensitivity, 3) latencyTier, 4) minQualityScore, 5) tenant prefixed overrides.
- Safe-fallback: if no profile satisfies minQualityScore and latencyTier, server returns HTTP 409 with structured error (see Error handling) unless fallbackPolicy == guarantee-min-quality, in which case server attempts higher-cost alternative and returns a pricing delta.

Error handling and client contract states
1) 400 Bad Request: malformed fidelityHint or invalid parameter values.
2) 409 Conflict: cannot satisfy constraints. Body includes suggested adjustments.
3) 412 Precondition Failed: tenant has not enabled negotiation or exceeded negotiation quota.
4) 502/503: platform capacity shortfall; negotiation may suggest queued execution or lower priority batch.

Observability and billing integration
- Telemetry: attach negotiationTraceId to all downstream execution spans and emitted tokens. Emit the following metrics per request: negotiation.duration_ms, negotiation.outcome (chosen_profile), negotiation.cost_multiplier, negotiation.rejections.{reason}.
- Logs: include fidelityHint and negotiation outcome in structured request logs (json) with PII redaction rules.
- Billing: effectivePriceMultiplier is multiplied against existing per-token/embedding unit price. For Dedicated tenants with committed pricing, multiplier may be ignored (documented per-tenant behavior returned in negotiation).

Security and privacy considerations
- Deny-listing: acceptableVariants must not leak internal-only model names to unauthorized tenants. Server should normalize display names in public logs.
- Data residency: negotiation decisions that reference regional capacity must not expose region identifiers beyond allowed tenant scope.

Compatibility and migration path
- Backwards compatibility: if fidelityHint is absent, server behaves exactly as today. New fields are additive.
- SDK changes: SDKs will include a FidelityHint builder helper and validation helpers.
- Migration doc: provide a one-page migration checklist for customers in product-overview (linked).

Rollout plan
1) Phase 0 (internal alpha, 4 weeks): server-side evaluation + simulated negotiation only. No client-facing change.
2) Phase 1 (partner beta, 6 weeks): opt-in toggle for selected Hosted customers. Provide /v1/fidelity-negotiate preflight endpoint.
3) Phase 2 (gradual public rollout, 8 weeks): default-enabled for pay-as-you-go customers with telemetry.
4) Phase 3 (enterprise toggle parity, 4 weeks): integrate with Dedicated/Private feature flags and contract clauses.

Monitoring and SLOs for negotiation service
- Availability: 99.95% for negotiation endpoint (target).
- Freshness: negotiation decisions must complete within 50ms p95 for realtime and 200ms p95 for interactive.
- Correctness: <0.1% of negotiation outcomes will be audited as mismatches between declared and observed quality (via periodic evals).

Operational runbook highlights
- If negotiation.duration_ms p99 > 1s, flip to conservative default profiles and open incident.
- If negotiation.rejections.rate > 0.5% baseline increase, notify product and throttle partner opt-ins.
- Escalation: own by Runtime Reliability -> paged after 15m sustained latency breach.

Appendix: Example negotiation sequences
1) Cheap embedder use-case: fidelityHint {costSensitivity: "high", latencyTier: "background", minQualityScore: 0.6} -> server picks quantized small model, multiplier 0.5.
2) Interactive chat requiring streaming: fidelityHint {costSensitivity: "low", latencyTier: "realtime", preferStreaming: true, minQualityScore: 0.9} -> server may select higher-cost variant, multiplier 1.4, or return 409 if unavailable.

Appendix: Example preflight endpoint (POST /v1/fidelity-negotiate)
Request: same body as /v1/infer but flagged preflight: true. Server returns negotiated profile and "estimatedCostDelta" and does not consume quota or bill.
